title: World Geography
lines: World geography questions in USAT-A ask about continents and oceans, the largest and longest features, countries with their capitals and currencies, famous landmarks, straits and canals, and lines of latitude and longitude. These facts change very slowly, which makes them ideal for revision tables.
- Seven continents, from largest to smallest: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia (Oceania).
- Asia is both the largest and the most populous continent. Australia is the smallest.
- Five oceans, from largest: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic. The Pacific is also the deepest; its Mariana Trench holds the deepest point on Earth.
| Highest mountain | Mount Everest, about 8,849 m, on the Nepal-China border
| Longest river | the Nile (usually given); the Amazon carries the most water
| France, Germany, Italy | Paris, Berlin, Rome | euro
! Many questions test the capital that is not the biggest city: Canberra not Sydney, Ottawa not Toronto, Ankara not Istanbul, Brasília not Rio de Janeiro, Abuja not Lagos.
| Statue of Liberty | New York, USA
| Strait of Gibraltar | Spain and Morocco; Atlantic and Mediterranean
| Bosphorus | Europe and Asia at Istanbul; Black Sea and Sea of Marmara
| Strait of Hormuz | Iran and Oman; Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
| Strait of Malacca | Malaysia and Sumatra; Indian Ocean and South China Sea
| Bab-el-Mandeb | Yemen and Djibouti; Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
| Bering Strait | Asia and North America
| Suez Canal (1869) | Mediterranean and Red Sea, in Egypt
- The Equator (0° latitude) divides north and south. The Tropic of Cancer (about 23.5° N) and Tropic of Capricorn (about 23.5° S) mark where the Sun can be directly overhead.
- The Prime Meridian (0° longitude) passes through Greenwich, London. The International Date Line runs roughly along 180°.
- The Earth turns 15° of longitude each hour, so places 15° apart differ by one hour of local time.
> Which strait links the Persian Gulf to the open sea?  (A) Malacca  (B) Hormuz  (C) Bosphorus  (D) Gibraltar
> B. Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and is a key route for oil tankers.
> The currency of Bangladesh is the  (A) rupee  (B) taka  (C) rupiah  (D) riyal
> B. The rupiah is Indonesia's currency, a common confusion with the rupee.
! The Sahara is the largest hot desert; Antarctica, a cold desert, is larger in area.
! The Caspian Sea is the largest lake, though it is salt water and called a sea.
! Mount Everest is the highest above sea level; K2 is second.
- Asia largest continent; Pacific largest and deepest ocean.
- Everest highest; Nile longest; Sahara largest hot desert; Russia largest country.
